title: N-able Research Finds AI Security Tools are Threatened by Trust and Complexity Challenges
summary: New global study finds as AI adoption accelerates, 75.5% of organizations still don’t fully trust AI-powered remediation without human review BURLINGTON, Massachusetts — October 15, 2026 — N-able, Inc. (NYSE:...
body_markdown:
*New global study finds a* *s AI adoption accelerates, 75.5% of organizations still don’t fully trust AI-powered remediation without human review*


**BURLINGTON, Massachusetts — October 15, 2026** —[N-able](https://www.n-able.com/)


, Inc. (NYSE: NABL), a global cybersecurity company delivering end-to-end business resilience, today released[“The AI Fog Report: When the Signal Becomes the Noise,”](https://www.n-able.com/resources/ai-fog-report-2026)


an independent global research report examining how small and medium size enterprises are scaling to drive business continuity during this new era of Frontier AI.


The survey of 595 cybersecurity decision-makers and practitioners across the United States and United Kingdom finds the security industry at an inflection point. As organizations rapidly adopt AI-powered security technologies, increasingly capable Frontier AI models are transforming both cyber defense and attacker capabilities.


The research reveals three critical challenges: AI is amplifying complexity within already complex security environments, security teams are struggling to separate context from noise to identify what matters most, and AI adoption is outpacing organizational trust and governance. Together, these trends are reshaping how organizations manage cyber risk and highlighting the need for greater context, confidence, and control.


“Security teams are entering the AI era from an already difficult operating position,” said Brendan Griffin, Director of Threat Research at N-able. “The promise of AI has never been greater, but simply adding more AI doesn’t automatically produce better security outcomes. Organizations need AI that reduces operational complexity, delivers meaningful context, and helps defenders make confident decisions faster.”


**AI is amplifying complexity inside already complex security environments**


- **1%**


of respondents report security alert volumes increased over the past 12 months, including


**24.2%**


who say alert volume increased by more than 50%.


- Among organizations experiencing increased alert volume, respondents most often attribute growth to


**adding more detection tools (40.2%)**


, followed by


**AI enabling attackers to launch attacks faster (26.2%)**


, while


**1%**


say multiple factors are contributing simultaneously.


-


**5%**


have


encountered


a confirmed or suspected AI-assisted attack during the past year, illustrating how AI is accelerating the pace and scale of modern threats.


-


**8%**


say alert noise interferes with incident response daily or several times each week, while only


**8.7%**


report that alert noise rarely or never affects operations.


The findings suggest organizations are reaching a point of diminishing returns from layering AI on their existing stacks. As adoption continues to grow, reducing operational friction and helping defenders focus on the decisions that matter most should be the core focus of AI security solutions.


**Security teams face a signal problem in addition to a volume problem**


- The leading sources of low-quality signal are


**duplicate alerts from overlapping tools (50.4%)**


and


**AI-generated alerts lacking sufficient context (48.9%)**


,


indicating


organizations increasingly struggle with interpretation rather than detection alone.


- **0%**


rank faster detection-to-containment as AI’s most valuable operational outcome.


- Respondents’ desired outcomes consistently emphasize


**better prioritization**


over


**more telemetry**


, reinforcing


that signal quality, not alert quantity, is becoming the industry’s defining challenge.


-


When asked what AI should


optimize


for, the largest share ( **8%** )


say


**both broader detection coverage and better signal precision are equally important**


, while


**32.6%**


prioritize broader detection and


**29.6%**


prioritize fewer, higher-confidence alerts.


**AI adoption is accelerating faster than organizational trust**


- **0%**


have meaningfully increased AI-powered security tool adoption during the past year, with another


**16.5%**


planning


to increase adoption over the next 12 months.


- Just **5%**


fully trust autonomous AI remediation, highlighting a significant gap between adoption and confidence.


- Yet **1%**


report making at least minor security policy exceptions to enable AI tools. Additionally, only


**51.9%**


maintain


a comprehensive inventory of AI tools


operating


across their environments.


- Before trusting autonomous AI, **7%** of respondents require full explainability. **59.8%** require there to be built-in human override.


-


Only **0%**


are


very confident


their existing security stack can keep pace with AI without a significant overhaul.


Boyd Smith, Founder and President,[TechKnowledgey](https://www.techknowledgeyinc.com/about-us/)


said, ” For many non-customer-facing roles, we’re embracing AI for its potential to transform how we operate. AI creates the most value when it helps our teams cut through complexity and focus on the threats that matter most, freeing them up to focus on people instead of running processes.”


The full findings of “When the Signal Becomes the Noise: The AI Fog Report,” are available here:[https://www.n-able.com/resources/ai-fog-report-2026](https://www.n-able.com/resources/ai-fog-report-2026)


.
